Definition: something brought near the altar, i.e. a sacrificial present
BiblicalUsage: If any man brings an offering to the LORD, it shall be of the cattle, of the herd or the flock, says Leviticus. The meat offering is fine flour with oil and frankincense, the princes bring their silver chargers full of it, and Ezekiel charges Israel with offering on every high hill. The word is the thing brought near the altar — the sacrificial present.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe an offering is a man bringing his best near to God, and the whole book of Leviticus is that one movement. I hold that every offering in the law points to the one who was offered once for all, and that is why the word matters.
